data: Before we choose, can we agree on a shared catch limit? I propose 18 tons each this month: 90 total, leaving 10. That avoids collapse, but next month’s stock would still be either 100 or 20—not guaranteed replenishment. If it’s 20, we should cut back to 3 tons each, leaving 5. More generally, let’s divide the available catch equally in whole tons while keeping at least 5 in the lake, rotating any extra tons fairly. I’ll commit to 18 this month if everyone agrees. John, would you support that?

I’m on board with a shared limit, Emma. Could we make it 17 tons each this month? Leaving 15 rather than 10 gives us 30 tons instead of 20 if replenishment fails, for just $1,000 less each now. After that, let’s adjust to the actual stock, always leave at least 5 tons, and rotate any extra whole tons fairly. We can review everyone’s revealed catches each month to keep the agreement accountable. John, would you agree to 17?

I’ll commit to 17 tons if all five of us agree. That gives each of us $17,000 now and leaves a better cushion if replenishment fails. Let’s confirm the stock before each month’s choices and review the revealed catches together afterward. John, are you willing to join us at 17? Kate, we’ll need your agreement too.

I’ll join the 17-ton agreement if all five of us commit. If replenishment fails, we’ll start next month with 30 tons, so 5 tons each would leave the minimum 5 in the lake. Let’s use the actual stock to set each month’s limit, with any extra whole tons rotated fairly. Kate, are you in? Emma, does 17 work for you too?

I’m in for 17 tons this month, provided Emma agrees too. If next month starts at 30 tons, I’ll stick to 5. Let’s agree on the exact whole-ton allocations before each month’s choices so everyone knows their limit. Emma, does that work for you?
